subtopic: FlashAttention / IO complexity and backward recomputation
learningObjective: Explain FlashAttention's core algorithmic idea: block-tiled attention with online softmax and backward recomputation of the attention matrix.

requiredFeatures: large SMEM for K, V, S tiles

stem: Which statement most accurately describes the algorithmic contribution of FlashAttention (as an exact attention algorithm)?

options.text: FlashAttention replaces softmax with a low-rank approximation whose rank is chosen per tile, reducing attention from O(N^2) to O(N sqrt(N)) FLOPs while remaining within an epsilon-approximation of exact attention.

FlashAttention keeps the attention math exact but reorders the computation into K/V-block tiles with an online softmax so the full N x N attention matrix is never materialized in HBM; in the backward pass the attention weights are recomputed from stored (m, l) statistics and Q, K, V rather than reloaded from HBM.

FlashAttention prunes tokens with attention weight below a learned threshold (sparse attention) and skips the corresponding tiles; correctness is preserved because the pruned weights are provably below numerical noise for typical language models.
FlashAttention rewrites attention in FP8 with per-row scale factors that let the softmax denominator be computed without dequantization; the FP8 arithmetic is the key to the wall-clock speedup.

explanation: FlashAttention is an IO-aware but exact attention algorithm. It tiles Q, K, V into blocks and computes softmax(QK^T)V per tile using the online softmax recurrence, so the N x N attention matrix S is never stored in HBM. Only per-row statistics (m, l) and the running output O are kept. In the backward pass, S and the softmax probabilities P are recomputed from Q, K, V and the stored (m, l), avoiding an HBM-resident P. This trades a small amount of extra compute (backward recomputation) for a large reduction in HBM I/O.

optionExplanations.B: Correct: exact algorithm + IO-aware tiling + backward recomputation.
optionExplanations.A: Wrong: FlashAttention is exact, not approximate; it does not change asymptotic FLOP count.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: FlashAttention is dense and exact; token pruning is a different (approximate) family.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: FlashAttention v1/v2 do not require FP8; the win is HBM I/O reduction, not lower precision.

assumptions: Discussion refers to FlashAttention v1/v2 exact attention (not FlashAttention-style approximate variants).
SMEM per SM is large enough to hold Q, K, V, and S tiles for the chosen block sizes.
nonImplications: Does not imply that FlashAttention is faster than a well-implemented naive attention on very short sequences.
Does not imply that the speedup is uniform across shapes; head dim, sequence length, and batch all matter.
